claims.claim_text: ARBs considered as an alternative when ACEis are not tolerated
In patients with advanced diabetic kidney disease, ACEIs were superior to ARBs in lowering risk of all-cause death but not in kidney events and cardiovascular events.
ACEIs were superior to ARBs and other antihypertensive drugs for the prevention of kidney events, cardiovascular outcomes, cardiovascular death and all-cause mortality.
a critical review of available evidence does not support a deleterious effect of RAS blockers in COVID-19 infections.
ACEIs and ARBs may be associated with lower incidence and/or improved outcome in patients with lower respiratory tract infections.
neither angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors (ACEIs) nor angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) reduced cardiovascular events and mortality in major trials in CKD.
